epic.intent:
Reverse engineer the available Aion 2 monster assets and bring the full available bestiary into Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord as functional creatures in FWGC++ generated campaigns. User confirmed full available bestiary on 2026-10-09. This is a follow-on implementation epic to FWGC++ procedural Bannerlord campaigns with War Sails (ep_01m4fpnf646t254mnh69jhz107), whose existing scope reuses native character assets. Preserve source creature appearance and usable source animation; implement Bannerlord behavior and world placement around verified engine capabilities. A display-only model, humanoid reskin substitution, or selected-monster demo does not complete the epic.

The bestiary denominator is every available monster in the inspected, pinned Aion 2 client/content set, including bosses and distinct variants, reconciled against an explicit inventory. It does not assume server-only or future unreleased assets are locally available. Record missing source dependencies and unsupported runtime features as incomplete entries; never silently narrow the roster. No client files, extraction route, creature count or Bannerlord nonhuman support have been verified during planning. This epic is backlog planning, not a completed extraction or running mod.

successCriteria.text: A pinned Aion 2 build/content inventory enumerates the full available bestiary with stable IDs, variants, meshes, materials, skeletons, animations and missing dependencies; inventory evidence makes omissions and duplicate records reviewable.

A repeatable local pipeline converts the inventoried creatures and their required dependencies into Bannerlord-ready assets, preserving source identity and recording provenance, source/build hashes and conversion settings.

Every inventoried creature has an accepted runtime result for its appearance, scale, animation, movement, attacks, damage reception and death. Unsupported skeletons, movement families, bosses or variants remain explicit unmet scope until resolved; a representative demo alone cannot pass.

Generated campaigns instantiate creatures through stable roster/encounter policies, valid habitat and navigation rules, and combat missions; every roster entry is reachable by a documented encounter or deterministic validation scenario without corrupting native human content.

Creature IDs, content versions, spawned state and encounter outcomes survive save/load and cold restart across two different generated worlds; missing or mismatched content is detected before invalid simulation or silent remapping.

A reproducible local package passes complete bestiary coverage checks, per-family runtime scenarios, visual inspection and measured campaign/battle performance against budgets established from the installed target. Failed entries remain failed rather than excluded from the completion denominator.

epic.title: Monster Mash: full Aion 2 bestiary for Bannerlord

bundle.rationale:
# Outcome and scope
Monster Mash is the user-requested follow-on epic to FWGC++ procedural Bannerlord campaigns with War Sails. The user explicitly chose the full available Aion 2 bestiary, not a selected first release. Include all observed monsters, bosses and distinct variants in the pinned available content set. Exact count and source formats are unknown. Preserve creature appearance and functional behavior in Bannerlord; a small demo is only a capability probe.

# Planning record and evidence
A1: Save a distinct backlog epic with full-bestiary success criteria and provenance to ep_01m4fpnf646t254mnh69jhz107. Verify through get_epic and the saved snapshot.
A2: Provide bounded tickets, owned output paths, dependencies and one acceptance criterion per work ticket. Verify through validate_plan and acceptance coverage readback.
A3: Preserve upstream/native-character scope and distinguish planned functionality from runtime evidence. Verify the explicit upstream gate and pending asset/runtime investigations.
Coordinator: current Codex session. Read-only dependency review: /root/epic_dependencies, completed; source snapshot rv_01m4fv5977ep1p08v91am83hta and its planning comments. All implementation tickets remain backlog. No game extraction or runtime validation was performed during epic planning. Proposed paths/APIs must be reconciled against inspected builds during execution.

# Execution shape
One sprint has four phases: inspect and prove capabilities; convert and implement creatures; integrate with generated campaigns; verify the complete roster and local package. Independent source/export work, engine probing and upstream verification can proceed separately. Per-ticket dependencies gate joins, especially family runtime support before full-bestiary conversion, and accepted upstream evidence before campaign registration. The final node verifies the assembled work and ends in one human checkpoint. No implementation run is started by this planning request.

# Upstream contract
The existing upstream plan excludes custom race/skeleton art and is currently backlog. Do not rewrite it. Provenance and ticket references are informational, not scheduler-enforced cross-epic dependencies. The upstream verification ticket must block dependent integration until MMR-1 has accepted runtime/package evidence. Reuse the delivered equivalents of MMR-27 identity policies, MMR-30 registry, MMR-32 roster/template resolution, MMR-34 spawning, MMR-36 graph validation, MMR-42 encounters and MMR-48/49/50 save compatibility. Frozen monster policies/resources extend RuntimeDerivedBundle semantics rather than mutating WorldContentId. MMR-65 topology governs campaign positions and proximity.

# Completeness and discovery
The inventory defines the denominator and preserves missing dependencies and unsupported families as failures. Every creature needs asset, visual, runtime and campaign-policy evidence. Representative family probes establish feasibility only. The full-inventory conversion ticket is deliberately large until observed data permits honest per-family exception tickets; split corrective work from actual failures without shrinking its completion denominator. No monster count, engine version, encryption behavior or extractor support is invented. Source-client availability and all unusual movement/rig support remain unknown.

# Ownership and verification
Each claimed ticket has one owner. No two workers mutate the same asset pipeline paths or shared game/editor simultaneously; handoff requires release, acknowledgement and state verification and does not complete required work. Limit concurrency to two and continue independent work after failures. Store original source assets outside tracked project outputs. Public publishing is outside this local integration request. Record exact versioned artifacts and targeted evidence; final acceptance checks all inventory rows, real gameplay, two-world persistence and measured performance. A failure in any required creature remains a failed epic requirement.

Keep original source files and local paths out of tracked project/public outputs; this work produces a local playable installation, and public redistribution is a separate decision. Verify package contents can resolve their dependencies without developer workspace paths. The final acceptance node installs this package into the isolated target and performs the assembled end-to-end demonstration; do not add a separate merge-only ticket.

All output paths are proposed implementation contracts, not existing files. Record exact input/build hashes and evidence. One assigned worker owns each mutable path and the live game/editor; transfers require explicit release and acknowledgment, and handoff is not completion. Use a per-creature coverage ledger keyed by source IDs; unsupported or failed entries stay incomplete. A family sample proves an approach, not full-bestiary completion.

reasoning.rationale: Requires bounded asset or runtime integration with observed evidence and explicit handling of unsupported cases.
